sources.finding: Specs create requirements/design/tasks files and schedule independent tasks in dependency waves; correctness testing and mobile parity have explicit limits.

sources.title: Cloud sessions
sources.locator: How sessions work; prerequisites; client matrix
sources.finding: Clients attach to the same remote session; disconnection does not stop work, approvals wait, and paid plans include cloud compute with a ten-session cap.

sources.title: Kiro Web
sources.finding: Web is a paid-plan cloud client with interactive, Spec and autonomous modes, cron schedules and a documented no-auto-merge boundary.

sources.title: Steering
sources.finding: Workspace and global steering have separate scopes; cloud use of local personal configuration requires opt-in upload.

sources.title: Crew quick start
sources.finding: Crew is a distinct local or user-hosted Gateway agent with persistent sessions, schedules, memory and a task runner.

sources.title: Local command sandbox
sources.finding: Kiro's optional local sandbox covers shell commands/children and optionally stdio MCP, excluding the agent and built-in file tools.

sources.title: Privacy and security
sources.finding: Supervised mode reviews file changes after writes and can revert them; it is explicitly not a security boundary.

sources.title: Kiro pricing
sources.locator: Plan cards; pooling; trial FAQ checked 7 November 2026
sources.finding: Free has fifty credits; paid individual tiers and pooled team seats differ in included credits. Add-ons cost $0.04/credit and taxes are excluded.

sources.title: Crew Agent Backends
sources.finding: Developer Mode enables Preview selection of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and other harnesses. Existing sessions retain their backend. Pi lacks Crew MCP tools; Codex requires sandboxing; Claude preapproved calls may bypass Crew audit.

sources.title: Crew Task Runner
sources.locator: Loop; Task IDs; Recovery; Approval gates; Dependencies
sources.finding: Crew decomposes Markdown specs into persistent task runs and step sessions. Up to three runs/parallel steps, per-run IDs/branches/worktrees, test/review/retry checkpoints, restart reconciliation and explicit approval gates are documented.

sources.title: Requirements-First Specs
sources.finding: Kiro generates requirements.md with acceptance criteria, design.md with architecture and testing strategy, and tasks.md with dependencies and optional/required work. Humans review and refine each phase.

sources.title: Analyze Requirements
sources.finding: IDE/CLI requirements analysis identifies logical contradictions, ambiguities, conflicting constraints and missing cases. Chat answers update requirements.md. Web does not yet offer this analysis.

sources.title: Kiro Memory
sources.finding: Memory is stored locally per user account and shared by IDE/CLI on the machine. It defaults off in IDE and has read-only/learn controls. Current subagents can read parent memory but cannot modify it.

sources.title: Kiro Data Protection
sources.finding: Individual/free usage may supply content for improvement by default. IDE/CLI telemetry and content have separate opt-outs. Enterprise improvement collection is off; admin reports remain separately controlled. Free inputs may be held up to sixty days for abuse detection.

sources.title: Kiro License
sources.finding: Kiro IDE and CLI are AWS Content under AWS agreements and the AWS IP License. Chromium is the IDE engine; Bun powers the CLI frontend. Dependency licenses do not license the main application as open source.

sources.title: Crew Running 24/7
sources.finding: Crew Gateway can run as a service or in Docker on user hardware, including an always-on remote Linux host while the laptop sleeps. Sandbox availability is checked before container agent execution.

sources.title: Kiro Authentication
sources.finding: IDE, CLI, Web and Mobile support IAM Identity Center or organization identity providers such as Okta/Entra. CLI also has a CI/headless API-key path.

sources.title: Kiro Privacy and Security
sources.finding: IDE supervised mode presents agent file changes for human review and approval, but is explicitly not a sandbox or access-control boundary.

sources.title: Kiro Mobile availability
sources.finding: Android is publicly available through Google Play for Android 10+. iPhone requires requested early access through TestFlight; the request page says only limited invitees receive access. Both use paid-plan cloud sessions.

sources.title: Crew phone browser access
sources.locator: Reach it from a laptop or phone; named HTTPS tunnel; lines 236-433
sources.finding: The shipped gateway documents opening its HTTPS dashboard URL on a phone, including a named tunnel or Tailscale Serve token link. This is the user-hosted Crew browser client, distinct from the native Kiro Mobile app.

sources.title: Crew external harness authentication
sources.locator: AgentAuthDeclaration for Codex and Claude Code, lines 503-551
sources.finding: Codex uses its own .codex/auth.json and native sign-in; Claude Code uses its own .claude/.credentials.json and native terminal sign-in. Both are own_credential_file entitlements, independent of Crew Kiro logout. This establishes reuse of each coding agent account through its native harness rather than an API-key-only wrapper.

The presence model distinguishes principals in one session and attribution labels multiple human authors in the same session. preview.py permits the owner to enable this released opt-in preview; this is distinct people sharing one Crew, not just same-account device access.

sources.title: Kiro pricing
sources.locator: Plan cards; credit pooling; FAQ (free trial, credits, add-on credits, eligible use, unused credits)
sources.finding: Free $0 with 50 credits/month; Pro $20 (1,000 credits), Pro+ $40 (2,000), Pro Max $100 (5,000), Power $200 (10,000) per user per month, USD; add-on credits $0.04 each. Credit pooling for teams of 2+: $20 per seat/month adding 500 credits per seat; admins set user, group and profile limits; credit pooling doesn't use overages, existing Enterprise subscriptions can keep overages. First upgrade to Pro: rest of month free plus 500 trial credits valid 12 months. A credit is a unit of work; credits per prompt vary by model and task. Subscriptions cover IDE, CLI, Web, Crew, ACP IDEs and CI automation; use through third-party automation harnesses that route requests outside Kiro's native interfaces is not permitted. Auto routing or a chosen OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI or open-weight model.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Cloud sessions
sources.locator: Info box; capability table; How cloud sessions work; Prerequisites
sources.finding: Cloud sessions are included in the plan with no separate charge for cloud compute; up to 10 concurrent cloud sessions. IDE, CLI, Web and Mobile create, resume and steer the same session; disconnecting a client doesn't stop the agent; history, repositories and sandbox file state persist and the transcript replays on reattach; approvals wait for the next client. Workflow progress and results return to the parent session. Sessions run in the profile's Region, us-east-1 or eu-central-1; Pro-family plan required.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Workflows
sources.locator: Intro; Start from the agent; recipes; Enable per client; structure (steps, loops, branches); Background delegation
sources.finding: Workflows are opt-in graphs of agent steps, sequences, loops and parallel branches generated from a prompt (approved before running) or saved as recipes; Kiro ships investigate, feature-pipeline and publish-pr recipes. Steps may set custom agents, models and effort; each step session can be paused, resumed or steered and revisited with follow-ups; progress and results return to the parent chat. If Workflows is absent from settings it is not yet available for the account. Example prompts can ask for a fresh worktree.

sources.title: Kiro docs: GitHub (Kiro Web)
sources.locator: Installation; Assigning tasks from GitHub issues; How the agent works with GitHub; Addressing PR feedback; Review pull requests in your session; Multiple users
sources.finding: The kiro label or a /kiro comment assigns an issue to the agent, which listens to issue comments; users assign only to repositories where they have write permission and others cannot assign on their behalf. The agent clones into its sandbox, creates a feature branch, commits with co-authors, opens PRs with detailed descriptions; /kiro all and /kiro fix address PR review comments and check feedback. PR files and diffs show under Reviews. If multiple users assign the same issue, separate tasks are created.

sources.title: Kiro docs: GitLab (Kiro Web)
sources.finding: Kiro Web adds GitLab projects to a session, makes changes and opens merge requests.

sources.finding: The IDE runs on macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), Windows 10/11 (x64, ARM64) and listed Linux distributions; the CLI on macOS, Windows 11 and Linux; Web in any modern browser. Kiro ships as a desktop IDE, a VS Code extension (VS Code 1.145+, local workspaces only), a CLI, a web app, a mobile app and Crew. In the IDE you open a folder to start a session.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Authentication

sources.title: Kiro docs: Agent Client Protocol

sources.finding: Crew sessions can run on Kiro CLI, Kiro Agent, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, goose or DeepSeek Harness backends; backends other than Kiro CLI are Experimental (Crew 0.10.0+).

sources.title: Kiro docs: Schedule (Kiro Web)
sources.locator: Intro; View your scheduled tasks; status and Edit
sources.finding: Scheduled tasks run a prompt against GitHub or GitLab repositories on a schedule in autonomous mode without starting a session (Pro plans and up); they can be disabled, re-enabled and edited.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Hook types
sources.finding: Hooks trigger on file, task, prompt-submit, agent-stop, session-start and tool-use events; file and task triggers run in IDE and CLI V3, Web runs the prompt, stop, session and tool triggers.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Crew quick start
sources.finding: Crew is an open-source personal agent that runs on the user's machine, a local container or a remote machine they control, with its gateway at localhost:5476; first launch installs kiro-cli and signs in.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Crew multi-instance
sources.finding: Crew can run chats on remote hosts, EC2, home servers or Fargate over SSH or SSM from one dashboard; opt-in, off by default, behind a feature preview.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Crew Slack
sources.finding: DM the Crew agent from Slack; each DM thread is a session with streaming replies and approval buttons.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Crew security
sources.finding: Crew blocks protected credential paths, masks credential locations from subprocesses with its OS sandbox, redacts credential patterns and records every decision in a security event log.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Crew Task Runner
sources.finding: The Task Runner decomposes a spec into steps, tests each, retries and commits per step.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Kiro Mobile
sources.finding: Native app on Android (Google Play) and iPhone (TestFlight early access) for Pro-family plans; starts, follows and steers cloud sessions.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Credit pooling
sources.finding: One shared credit pool with no overages; seats $20/month add 500 credits; admins cap credits per user, with group and profile limits as fallbacks.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Cancelling your subscription
sources.finding: Cancelling means switching to Kiro Free; mid-month you keep the plan until month end and are not charged after.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Export sessions
sources.finding: Any IDE chat exports as a zip with prompts, responses, tool calls and code blocks.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Deleting your account
sources.finding: Deleting the account cancels subscriptions; it can be restored within 30 days, after which account and data are permanently deleted.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Prompt logging
sources.finding: Admins can log IDE and CLI prompts and responses to an S3 bucket in their own account.

sources.title: Kiro docs: User activity
sources.finding: Admins export per-user activity, including credit and overage use, as daily CSV to S3, daily OpenTelemetry metrics or real-time OpenTelemetry events.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Data protection
sources.locator: AWS regions where content is stored
sources.finding: Free and individual subscriber content is stored in us-east-1; enterprise content may be stored in the profile's Region; inference location can differ.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Compliance validation
sources.finding: Kiro is in the scope of AWS's ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, verified by EY CertifyPoint; reports download through AWS Artifact, which requires Builder ID or IAM Identity Center sign-in.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Enterprise support
sources.finding: With an AWS Support plan including Kiro Enterprise support, cases go through AWS Support or the Kiro Support power.

sources.title: Kiro CLI changelog 3.0.0
sources.locator: V3 by Default, Classic and Desktop App Retired; Breaking changes
sources.finding: CLI 3.0.0 (2026-11-03) made V3 default and retired the Classic interface, desktop app and inline autocomplete as breaking changes with migration notes; cloud sessions resume from /sessions.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Kiro Web
sources.finding: Kiro Web chats in a default collaborative mode, spec mode or autonomous mode and opens PRs or MRs; it never merges automatically.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Autonomous mode
sources.finding: Autonomous can be toggled before the first message or at any later point in the session.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Sandbox
sources.finding: Each task runs in its own isolated sandbox whose file state is kept with the session until the session is deleted.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Sandbox internet access
sources.finding: Network levels: connections only, common dependencies or open internet, plus a custom domain allow-list.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Sandbox environment variables
sources.finding: Environment variables and encrypted secrets are exposed to the sandbox; docs warn the agent may exfiltrate secrets.

sources.title: Kiro docs: Sandbox environment configuration
sources.finding: The Web agent detects the project type and configures the sandbox from manifests such as package.json or requirements.txt.
